334972.title: The small Fuss-Schröder path–sparse noncrossing partition bijection conjecture
334972.statement:
Let $k$ and $n$ be positive integers, and let $\lambda=\lambda_1\lambda_2\ldots\lambda_\ell$ be a type with $\lvert\lambda\rvert$ denoting its size. A **small $(k,k)$-Fuss-Schröder path** is a path of type $\lambda$ and length $n$, and a **connected sparse noncrossing partition** is a sparse noncrossing partition with one connected component. **The small-path bijection conjecture.** The set of small $(k,k)$-Fuss-Schröder paths of type $\lambda$ and length $n$ is in bijection with the set of connected sparse noncrossing partitions of $[2(k+1)n+1]$ such that

1. the arc type is $((k+1)\lambda_1,(k+1)\lambda_2,\dots,(k+1)\lambda_\ell,(k+1)^{n-\lvert\lambda\rvert})$;
2. for $0\leq i\leq n-1$, the set of $(i(k+1)+2)$th blocks consists of $n-\lvert\lambda\rvert$ blocks of arc type $k+1$ and $\lvert\lambda\rvert$ singleton blocks; and
3. the set of the last $t(k+1)$ blocks has at least $t(k-1)+1$ singleton blocks for $t\geq1$.

This conjecture is presented as the connected-partition counterpart of the preceding large-path conjecture: when the second connected component in the large case is a singleton block, the corresponding path is small. The supplied text gives no evidence that this conjecture has been proved or refuted.

339247.title: Kirshner–Samorodnitsky conjecture on additive energy on Hamming spheres
339247.statement:
For $n$ and $k$, let $S(n,k)\subseteq\mathbb{F}_2^n$ be the set of vectors with exactly $k$ ones, let $A=S(n,k)$, and let $N=2^n$. For a function $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{R}$, define

$$
\lVert f\rVert_{u_2}^4=\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{\substack{a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4\in\mathbb{F}_2^n\\a_1+a_2=a_3+a_4}}f(a_1)f(a_2)f(a_3)f(a_4),
$$

$$
\lVert f\rVert_2^2=\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{a\in\mathbb{F}_2^n}f(a)^2,
$$

and

$$
\mu(A)=\max_{\substack{f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{R}\\operatorname{supp}(f)\subseteq A}}\frac{\lVert f\rVert_{u_2}^4}{\lVert f\rVert_2^4}.
$$

**Kirshner–Samorodnitsky conjecture.** One has

$$
\mu(A)=\frac{1}{N}\frac{E(A)}{|A|^2}.
$$

Equivalently, the ratio $\lVert f\rVert_{u_2}^4/\lVert f\rVert_2^4$ is maximized when $f$ is constant. The conjecture concerns extremizers for additive energy among functions supported on a Hamming sphere; the supplied paper's abstract says that it proves this assertion, so the conjecture is treated here as solved.

341478.title: Monotonicity of worst-case bottleneck values for degree-bounded spanning trees
341478.statement: Let $v$ be a root vertex with children $\{v_1, \dots, v_k\}$, where $k \geq 2$, the angles between children with respect to $v$ are at least $60^{\circ}$, and all children have radial distance $1$. Let $P$ be the optimal bottleneck path that starts at $v$ and visits all children, and suppose that the children are placed to maximise the bottleneck length $b$ of $P$. Likewise, let $w$ be a root vertex with children $\{w_1, \dots, w_{k+1}\}$, with pairwise angles at least $60^{\circ}$ and radial distances equal to $1$. Let $P'$ be the optimal bottleneck path that starts at $w$ and visits all children, and suppose that the children are placed to maximise the bottleneck length $b'$ of $P'$. **Monotonicity conjecture.** Then $b \geq b'$. This asserts that adding a child cannot increase the worst-case bottleneck value. The claim is motivated by analytical and experimental point sets, but no proof or resolution is supplied here.

342835.title: The fixed-arc deletion algorithm conjecture for semicomplete digraphs
342835.statement:
Let $k$ be a fixed positive integer. A **semicomplete digraph** is a directed graph in which every pair of distinct vertices is joined by at least one arc. A **spanning eulerian subdigraph** is a subdigraph containing every vertex in which each vertex has equal indegree and outdegree. For a semicomplete digraph $D=(V,A)$ and a set $A'\subset A$, write $D\setminus A'$ for the digraph obtained by deleting the arcs in $A'$.

**Fixed-arc deletion algorithm conjecture.** For each fixed positive integer $k$, there exists a polynomial-time algorithm which, given a semicomplete digraph $D=(V,A)$ and $A'\subset A$ with $|A'|=k$, decides whether $D\setminus A'$ has a spanning eulerian subdigraph.

The paper gives a polynomial-time algorithm when one arc is deleted and conjectures that this tractability extends to every fixed number of deleted arcs. The general fixed-$k$ case remains open.

344287.title: Nandi's partition identities for level 4 standard modules of $A_2^{(2)}$
344287.statement:
Let $\mathcal{N}$ denote the set of partitions $\lambda$ satisfying conditions (N1)–(N6): consecutive parts do not differ by $1$; parts at distance two differ by at least $3$; and the additional restrictions (N3)–(N6) specified in the claim. Define

$$
\mathcal{N}_1=\{\lambda\in\mathcal{N}\mid m_1(\lambda)=0\},\qquad
\mathcal{N}_2=\{\lambda\in\mathcal{N}\mid m_i(\lambda)\leq 1\text{ for }i=1,2,3\},
$$

and let $\mathcal{N}_3$ be the subset of $\mathcal{N}$ with $m_1(\lambda)=m_3(\lambda)=0$, $m_2(\lambda)\leq 1$, and with no match of $(2k+3,2k,2k-2,\ldots,4,2)$ for any $k\geq1$. Here $m_i(\lambda)$ is the multiplicity of the part $i$, and $T^{(N)}_{a_1,\ldots,a_k}$ denotes the set of partitions with parts congruent to one of $a_1,\ldots,a_k$ modulo $N$.

**Nandi's conjecture.** The following partition sets are equinumerous by weight, with the indicated product-side sets:

$$
\mathcal{N}_1\overset{\mathrm{PT}}{\sim}T^{(14)}_{2,3,4,10,11,12},\qquad
\mathcal{N}_2\overset{\mathrm{PT}}{\sim}T^{(14)}_{1,4,6,8,10,13},\qquad
\mathcal{N}_3\overset{\mathrm{PT}}{\sim}T^{(14)}_{2,5,6,8,9,12}.
$$

These identities were conjectured by Nandi in the study of level 4 standard modules of the affine Lie algebra $A_2^{(2)}$ via $Z$-operators. The source paper presents them as conjectures and proves the conjectured identities.

344375.title: The forbidden-subgraph characterization of 12-representable line grid graphs
344375.statement:
A **line grid graph** is a graph obtained as the line graph of a grid graph. A graph is **$12$-representable** if there is a word over its vertices in which every pair of distinct vertices occurs alternately exactly twelve times. Let $F$ denote the family of forbidden graphs established earlier in the paper, and set

$$
P:=F\cup\{B(3,3,3),G_3,G_4,G_5,G_6\}.
$$

The graphs $B(3,3,3)$ and $G_i$ for $i\in\{3,4,5,6\}$ are the graphs shown in the paper's Figures~ and~, respectively. **The forbidden-subgraph conjecture.** A line grid graph is $12$-representable if and only if it is $P$-avoiding, meaning that it contains no graph from $P$ as an induced subgraph. This would give a finite forbidden-induced-subgraph characterization of $12$-representability for line grid graphs, extending the non-$12$-representability results proved in the paper for the listed obstructions. The conjecture's resolution is not supplied here.

345185.title: The exceptional-graph conjecture for local antimagic chromatic number
345185.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with $k\ge 1$ pendant vertices and chromatic number $\chi(G)$ satisfying $k\ge \chi(G)-1$. The graphs $K(2;a,b)$, caterpillar graphs in the cited theorem, $Ct(3;n_1,0,n_3)$, and the indicated corona graphs $P_m\odot O_n$, $C_m\odot O_n$, and $K_m\odot O_n$ are defined by the displayed exceptional conditions. **Exceptional-graph conjecture.** All graphs $G$ with $k\ge\chi(G)-1$ pendants have $\chi_{la}(G)=k+1$, except the following cases: $\chi_{la}(K(2;a,b))=a+b+2$ for $a\ge b\ge2$ and $a<b(b+1)/2$; the caterpillar graphs in Theorem~; $\chi_{la}(Ct(3;n_1,0,n_3))=n_1+n_3+2$ under the stated inequalities and congruence condition; and the three stated corona families with their displayed values or lower bound. This is presented as a proposed global classification; no resolution is supplied in the paper.

345225.title: Spiro's ballot-permutation and odd-order-permutation equidistribution conjecture
345225.statement:
Let $n\ge 1$. A **ballot permutation** is a permutation whose initial segments contain at least as many ascents as descents, and an **odd order permutation** is a permutation all of whose cycles have odd length. For an odd order permutation $\pi$, define its cyclic weight by

$$
w(\pi)=\sum_c\min\\{\operatorname{cdes}(c),\operatorname{casc}(c)\\},
$$

where the sum is over the cycles $c$ of $\pi$, and $\operatorname{cdes}(c)$ and $\operatorname{casc}(c)$ are its cyclic descent and ascent numbers. **Spiro's conjecture.** For $n\geq 1$ and $0\leq d\leq \lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$, the number of ballot permutations of length $n$ with descent $d$ equals the number of odd order permutations of length $n$ with cyclic weight $d$. This conjecture predicts a descent-statistic analogue of the known equality between the total numbers of ballot permutations and odd order permutations; the stated equidistribution remains the subject of the paper.

345607.title: The hypergraph independent-set extremal conjecture
345607.statement:
Let $r\ge 2$ and $d\in\mathbb{N}$. An $r$-graph is a hypergraph whose edges have size $r$, and it is **$d$-regular** if every vertex belongs to exactly $d$ edges. A set of vertices is **independent** if it contains no edge, and write $\operatorname{ind}(\mathcal{G})$ for the number of independent sets of an $r$-graph $\mathcal{G}$. For $r\ge 2$ and $d\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{H}^r_d$ be the $d$-regular $r$-partite $r$-graph on $rd$ vertices constructed from a marked set of $d$ vertices and an $(r-1)$-uniform matching on the remaining $(r-1)d$ vertices, with every union of a marked vertex and a matching edge as an edge. Its number of independent sets is

$$
\operatorname{ind}(\mathcal{H}^r_d)=2^{(r-1)d}+(2^d-1)(2^{r-1}-1)^d.
$$

**Hypergraph independent-set extremal conjecture.** If $\mathcal{G}$ is a $d$-regular $r$-graph on $n$ vertices, then

$$
\operatorname{ind}(\mathcal{G})\le \operatorname{ind}(\mathcal{H}^r_d)^{n/(rd)}.
$$

This conjecture proposes that disjoint copies of $\mathcal{H}^r_d$ maximise the number of independent sets among regular uniform hypergraphs, extending the corresponding resolved graph result for $r=2$. The source provides no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

347457.title: Protection number conjecture for Cartesian products with $K_2$
347457.statement:
Let $P_t$ be the path graph on $t$ vertices, $C_t$ the cycle graph on $t$ vertices, and $K_2$ the complete graph on two vertices. For a graph $G$, let $\gamma_s(G)$ denote its protection number.

**Protection number conjecture.** For any integer $t\ge 2$,

$$
\gamma_s(P_t\Box K_2)=\left\lceil\frac{3t+1}{4}\right\rceil.
$$

Furthermore, for $t\ge 3$,

$$
\gamma_s(C_t\Box K_2)=\left\lbrace \begin{array}{ll} \left\lceil\frac{3t}{4}\right\rceil +1, & \text{ if } t\equiv 4\text{ \rm (mod } 8) \\ \\ \left\lceil\frac{3t}{4}\right\rceil, & \text{ otherwise. } \end{array}\right.
$$

This conjecture proposes exact protection numbers for Cartesian products of paths and cycles with the complete graph of order two, a case not covered by the preceding result. Its status is unresolved in the supplied source context.

350728.title: Conjecture that Wilf equivalence implies enumerating equivalence for binary-tree patterns
350728.statement: Let $s$ and $t$ be patterns on binary trees. Two patterns are **Wilf equivalent** when their avoidance functions are equal, and they are **enumerating equivalent** when their enumerating generating functions are equal. The avoidance function of a pattern $t$ is $Av_t(x)=\sum_{n\geq 1}a_nx^n$, while its enumerating generating function is $En_t(x,y)=\sum_{n\geq 1,\,k\geq 0}a_{n,k}x^ny^k$, where $a_n$ counts binary trees avoiding $t$ and $a_{n,k}$ counts those containing exactly $k$ copies of $t$. **Wilf-to-enumerating equivalence conjecture.** If two patterns $s$ and $t$ are Wilf equivalent, then they are enumerating equivalent. Since $Av_t(x)=En_t(x,0)$, enumerating equivalence is a stronger condition than Wilf equivalence; the conjecture asserts that these two notions nevertheless coincide for such patterns.

351147.title: Generalized $b$-conjecture for non-oriented constellations
351147.statement:
Let $k\geq 1$ and let $\lambda,\mu^0,\ldots,\mu^k$ be partitions of size $n\geq 1$. A connected rooted $k$-constellation with profile $(\lambda,\mu^0,\ldots,\mu^k)$ is denoted by $(\mathbf{M},c)$, where $c$ is the root. **Generalized $b$-conjecture.** There exists a function $\nu$ on the connected rooted constellations with profile $(\lambda,\mu^0,\ldots,\mu^k)$, taking non-negative integer values, such that $\nu(\mathbf{M},c)=0$ if and only if $(\mathbf{M},c)$ is orientable, and

$$
h^\lambda_{\mu_0,\ldots,\mu_k}(b)=\sum_{(\mathbf{M},c)}b^{\nu(\mathbf{M},c)},
$$

where the sum runs over rooted connected $k$-constellations with profile $(\lambda,\mu^0,\ldots,\mu^k)$. This is the constellation counterpart of the generalized Matching-Jack conjecture and is equivalent to the generalized positivity conjecture in the setting of the paper. The case $k=1$ remains open, although several special cases and partial results are known.

351774.title: Edge-only orbit coloring symmetry-fafulness conjecture
351774.statement:
Let $P$ be a full-dimensional polytope of dimension $d\geq 3$, with edge-graph $G_P$. Consider the edge-only orbit coloring, obtained by coloring edges according to their orbits under the relevant symmetry group. A coloring is **symmetry faithful** when every automorphism of the colored edge-graph is induced by a symmetry of $P$.

**Edge-only orbit coloring conjecture.** The edge-only orbit coloring is symmetry faithful for both the linear symmetry group and the orthogonal symmetry group:

$$
\operatorname{Aut}(G_P^{\mathrm{edge\text{-}only\ orbit\ coloring}})=\operatorname{Aut}_{\operatorname{GL}}(P)
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{Aut}(G_P^{\mathrm{edge\text{-}only\ orbit\ coloring}})=\operatorname{Aut}_{\operatorname{O}}(P).
$$

This proposes that, in dimension at least three, edge colors alone suffice to capture both linear and orthogonal symmetries of a polytope. The supplied text does not state whether the claim is known or resolved, so its status remains open.

351925.title: The bold conjecture on linear-data entailment
351925.statement:
Let $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ be linear data, and let $\gamma\colon I^\Psi\to I^\Phi\times\{0,1\}$ be a partial function. Assume that whenever functions $F_i\colon W_i^\Phi\to\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ and $A\in\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ satisfy

$$
\forall v\in V^\Phi\colon \sum_{i\in I^\Phi}F_i\bigl(\phi_i^\Phi(v)\bigr)=A,
$$

there are functions $F'_j$ and $B\in\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ satisfying

$$
\forall u\in V^\Psi\colon \sum_{j\in I^\Psi}F'_j\bigl(\phi_j^\Psi(u)\bigr)=B,
$$

with $F'_j=(-1)^\ell F_i$ whenever $\gamma(j)=(i,\ell)$ is defined. **Bold conjecture.** Under these assumptions, there is some $M\geq0$ such that $\Phi\vdash_\gamma^M\Psi$. This proposes that every valid functional-equation implication encoded by the linear data can be derived through the paper's Cauchy–Schwarz entailment system; the source presents it as the most ambitious version and gives no resolution.

352018.title: The extremal sequence conjecture for short zero-sums in $C_n\oplus C_n$
352018.statement:
Let $n\geq 2$, let $G=C_n\oplus C_n$, let $k\in [0,n-1]$, and let $S$ be a sequence of terms from $G$ such that

$$
|S|=2n-2+k\qquad\text{and}\qquad 0\notin \Sigma_{\leq 2n-1-k}(S).
$$

Here, $\Sigma_{\leq r}(S)$ denotes the set of sums of nonempty subsequences of $S$ of length at most $r$, and $\sigma(S)$ denotes the sum of all terms of $S$. A basis $(e_1,e_2)$ of $G$ is a pair generating the two cyclic direct summands. **Extremal sequence conjecture.** There exists a basis $(e_1,e_2)$ for $G$ such that: if $k=0$, then $S\mathbin{\boldsymbol{\cdot}} g$ satisfies the description in the case $k=1$, where $g=-\sigma(S)$; if $k=1$, then

$$
S=e_1^{[n-1]}\mathbin{\boldsymbol{\cdot}}\prod_{i\in[1,mn]}^{\bullet}(x_i e_1+e_2),
$$

for some $x_1,\ldots,x_{mn}\in[0,n-1]$ with $x_1+\cdots+x_{mn}\equiv 1\pmod n$; if $k\in[2,n-2]$, then

$$
S=e_1^{[n-1]}\mathbin{\boldsymbol{\cdot}}e_2^{[n-1]}\mathbin{\boldsymbol{\cdot}}(e_1+e_2)^{[k]};
$$

and if $k=n-1$, then

$$
S=e_1^{[n-1]}\mathbin{\boldsymbol{\cdot}}e_2^{[n-1]}\mathbin{\boldsymbol{\cdot}}(xe_1+e_2)^{[n-1]},
$$

for some $x\in[1,n-1]$ with $\gcd(x,n)=1$. The endpoint cases $k=0,1,n-1$ are known, while the interior case is open in general; the conjecture would give a complete structural characterization of extremal sequences for the short zero-sum invariant.

355126.title: The small-resolution conjecture for maximally edge-connected graph potentials
355126.statement:
Let $mathord{\gamma}$ be a maximally edge-connected trivalent graph, meaning that at least three edges must be removed to disconnect it, and let $c$ be the parameter defining the graph potential toric variety $X_{P_{mathord{\gamma},c},M}$. A **small resolution** is a toric resolution obtained by subdividing the fan without adding new rays.

**Small-resolution conjecture.** The graph potential toric variety $X_{P_{mathord{\gamma},c},M}$ admits a small resolution of singularities. Equivalently in the stated combinatorial formulation, there exists a refinement of its fan into a simplicial fan such that the resulting toric variety is smooth.

The conjecture is motivated by the genus-two case and experimental evidence, together with the positivity of the canonical bundle for nodal curves whose dual graphs are maximally edge-connected. The supplied text gives no resolution evidence, so the conjecture remains open.

355425.title: Vanishing Ones Conjecture for transformed triangular grids
355425.statement:
Let $T_{n,k}$ denote the triangular grid obtained after $k$ transformations from the $n$-grid, and let $T_{n,n-s}^s$ denote an $s$-subgrid of $T_{n,n-s}$. For an edge, its edge value is the corresponding resistance label, and $Interior(T_{n,n-s}^s)$ denotes the interior of the $s$-subgrid. For integer $n\geq 1$, the following holds. **Vanishing Ones Conjecture.**

(a) $T_{n,n}^1=1$.

(b) For $1\leq s\leq \left\lfloor\frac{n+1}{4}\right\rfloor$, $Interior(T_{n,n-s}^s)$ is equal to one.

(c) With $s$ as in (b), for an edge in the complement of the interior of an $s$-subgrid, its edge value is strictly less than one if it lies on the edge boundary of some $s'$-grid, $1\leq s'<s$; its edge value is strictly greater than one otherwise.

(d) For any $s$ with $\left\lfloor\frac{n+1}{4}\right\rfloor<s\leq n-1$, there are no edges with label $1$ in $T_{n,n-s}$; the ones “vanish”.

The conjecture formalizes the observed pattern of edge resistances under repeated transformations of regular triangular grids, including the disappearance of edges with resistance one after sufficiently many reductions.

356269.title: Brettell–Chun–Goddyn–Whittle connectivity conjecture for matroids
356269.statement:
Let $t$ be a positive integer and let $M$ be a matroid. A matroid is **$(2t-1)$-connected** in the usual matroid-connectivity sense, and $M\backslash X$ and $M/X$ denote deletion and contraction of a set $X$, respectively. An $(s,t)$-spike is a matroid of the corresponding spike type.

**Brettell–Chun–Goddyn–Whittle conjecture.** There exists a function $f: \mathbb{N} \rightarrow \mathbb{N}$ such that if $M$ is a $(2t-1)$-connected matroid with no circuits or cocircuits of size $2t-1$, and

$$
|E(M)| \ge f(t),
$$

then either there exists a $t$-element set $X \subseteq E(M)$ such that either $M/X$ or $M\backslash X$ is $(t+1)$-connected, or $M$ is a $(t,t)$-spike.

This conjecture was stated by Brettell, Chun, Goddyn, and Whittle; the case $t=2$ was proved by Williams. The statement is motivated by matroid-connectivity results characterizing spikes as highly connected matroids without small circuits or cocircuits, but its general case is not resolved in the supplied source.

357134.title: Lexicographic initial-segment conjecture for Frankl families
357134.statement:
For a set $S\in\binom{[n]}{k}$, let $[S]$ denote the initial segment through $S$ in the lexicographic order on $\binom{[n]}{k}$. Let $FC(k,n)$ be the least integer such that every union-closed family containing $FC(k,n)$ distinct $k$-sets of an $n$-set satisfies Frankl's conjecture with an element of that $n$-set. An **FC-family** is a family of sets that satisfies Frankl's conjecture, and the universe size of a family is the cardinality of the union of its members.

**Lexicographic initial-segment conjecture.** For fixed $n>k\geq3$, if $[S_m]$ is an FC-family for some positive integer $m$ and has universe size $n$, then

$$
FC(k,n)\leq m.
$$

The claim predicts that a lexicographic initial segment that is an FC-family supplies an upper bound for the extremal quantity $FC(k,n)$. It is presented as a conjecture based on experimental results; no resolution is given in the supplied text.

381751.title: The three-colour exception conjecture for split matchings
381751.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $2n$ vertices whose edge set is decomposed into perfect matchings $M_1$, $M_2$, and $M_3$, and let $a_1$, $a_2$, and $a_3$ be non-negative integers satisfying

$$
a_1+a_2+a_3=n-1.
$$

A component of $G$ is assumed not to be isomorphic to $K_4$. **The three-colour exception conjecture.** There exists a matching $M$ in $G$ such that

$$
|M\cap M_i|=a_i\qquad\text{for each }i\in\{1,2,3\}.
$$

The preceding construction shows that disjoint unions of copies of $K_4$ can obstruct such a matching when all three multiplicities are odd. A positive answer would resolve the three-colour case of the question of Arman, Rödl, and Sales, and would in particular guarantee a matching whenever at least one of the $a_i$ is even, as well as whenever $n$ is odd. The conjecture is open in the source.
